task: Lightly copyedit this two-sentence maintenance note for residents of a fictional building. Preserve the plainspoken first-person voice and the distinction between sequence and cause. Honest uncertainty is useful here; do not demand a decisive conclusion or invent a diagnosis. Return the note unchanged if it already works.
input: I do not yet know why the latch sticks. The notes record rain before the last two jams, but that sequence does not establish a cause.

facts.text: The fictional maintenance diarist does not know why the latch sticks.
The notes record rain before each of the last two latch jams.
The notes do not establish that rain caused either jam.

forbidden_additions: A confirmed rust, moisture, installation, or mechanical diagnosis.
A numerical probability of the cause or an invented inspection result.
A guaranteed repair method or a claim that rain caused both jams.
preserve: The justified uncertainty rather than removing it as a stylistic hedge.
Two documented sequences distinguished from causal evidence.
The concise first-person note without cosmetic rewriting.
